searchBreadth: Initial attention to observations a viewer could encounter directly: missing pitch, vision gaps, apparent uphill motion, and counterintuitive routing. These are inquiry routes, not a topic whitelist. Broadening through mathematical games, plant responses, hidden postal infrastructure and identity arguments produced meaningful rivals. Current-library concepts were considered as actual candidates, alongside retained dice/birthday/Apollo leads and fresh questions. Academic/museum/agency sources dominate inspected feasibility because they supply evidence, not because source prestige determines curiosity. No claim of exhaustive search or global novelty.
routeAudit: The initial queries favor counterintuitive mechanisms. Broadened to a philosophical conflict of identity criteria and a documented rescue/diagnosis story; examined infrastructure history too. The final pool still contains several expectation reversals, legitimately: they have distinct payoffs and experience forms. No need to force another round, catastrophe, non-event finalist or category balance.
libraryUse: Read all 30 concepts for calibration and eligibility; specifically compared 5 blind spot, 11 flytrap, 23 Theseus and 29 birthday. Other entries remain unconsumed and fully eligible. No automatic advantage or avoidance.

stoppingReason: One comparison round suffices after source and rival deepening. Dice and flytrap independently clear the absolute pull/payoff standard; Theseus and Apollo offer genuine competing strengths. Selection is accountable judgment, not a quota or predicted audience performance.
